history.summary: A well-built 2016 family condo (892 units, reputable Hong Realty/Architects 61) offering a large 1,389 sqft 3BR at $1,440 psf — ~8% under the $1,561 district median. Strong 6.9%/yr resale CAGR over a thick 206-transaction base, with Pasir Ris's CRL + DTL extension and the Pasir Ris Central redevelopment as forward catalysts.
history.rating_rationale: This is the most data-backed entry in the batch: 206 URA resale transactions giving a high-confidence 6.9%/yr CAGR, on a modern (2016) well-maintained 892-unit development at a $1,440 psf discount to the $1,561 median. Build quality and management reviews are positive after ~8 years. Sub-mid-$2M for a 1,389 sqft 3BR keeps it in the deep buyer band. Held below Strong Buy by the 750m (9-min) MRT walk — fine but not doorstep — and by OCR-far-east location capping the appreciation ceiling versus RCR peers.

catalysts: Cross Island Line (CRL, ~2030) interchange at Pasir Ris plus DTL extension — meaningful connectivity uplift
Pasir Ris Central integrated redevelopment (bus interchange, retail, polyclinic) lifting the whole node
Modern, well-managed 892-unit base with reputable developer — broad family/upgrader appeal

history.summary: CDL-built Pasir Ris condo where the asking $1,284 psf is verifiably below the entire last-12-month transaction range, backed by a deep 206-txn appreciation history - the cleanest value case of this batch.
history.rating_rationale: Asking $1,284 psf ($899k, 700 sqft, the larger end of the 1BR pool) is below the verified last-12-month range of $1,331-$1,606 psf (avg ~$1,538) per EdgeProp/PropertyGuru, so the very_low_psf flag is a genuine bargain on the larger 1BR layout, not a mis-scrape. The appreciation evidence is deep (206 txns) and the development is a well-regarded 892-unit CDL project, reducing data-quirk risk. D18/Pasir Ris is OCR, the region with the strongest realized forward returns (~+4.0%) in the backtest. Confidence is medium not high because the larger 700 sqft 1BR commands a structurally lower psf than shoebox 1BRs (part of the discount is a size effect) and leasehold from 2010 keeps it a pure-yield play.

99-yr leasehold from 2010, ~83 years remaining - no tenure edge
Pasir Ris is far-east; exit demand depends on CRL delivery
catalysts: Asking below the full recent transaction range = verified entry discount
Cross Island Line at Pasir Ris targeted 2030 improves connectivity
OCR location aligns with the strongest realized forward-return region (~+4.0%)

history.summary: A 893 sqft 'compact 3BR' (in fact a 2+study, 2-bath) at The Palette, Pasir Ris Grove, asking $1.30M / $1,456 psf. The price is genuinely good: it sits $50-95k BELOW every one of the 5 same-layout URA prints of the last 15 months ($1,350k-$1,370k, $1,511-$1,533 psf) and below the low-floor one too, so the ~5% discount survives the fact that this DB cannot tell us the unit's floor. What it buys, though, is the weakest product in a crowded enclave: eight identical compact-3BR asks are live in this project right now, D'Nest next door sells a 936 sqft 3BR for the same money, and the project's own tape has been flat for 18 months (+1.1% over the trailing year). Good entry, unexciting engine - fair, not a bargain.
history.rating_rationale: THE PRICE IS RIGHT, THE ASSET IS AVERAGE. Verified value: the 893.4 sqft layout is the project's second-deepest (19 of 206 URA prints) and printed Mar-25 $1,368k, May-25 $1,350k (floor 1-5), Sep-25 $1,360k, Apr-26 $1,368k, May-26 $1,370k; the 882.6 sqft sibling printed $1,395k in Apr-26. At $1.30M this ask is 4-7% under all of them, on a 9-print 24-month cohort - not a thin-cohort or mis-scrape artifact, and it clears even the worst-case low-floor adjustment (project floor factor 0.958 -> $1,467 psf fair = $1,310k). That is a real ~5% head start. But the lever that actually predicts forward returns reads NEUTRAL: vs age-adjusted D18 peers the unit is -0.4% - dead fair value, not cheap. The algo's 795 and its 7.1%/yr ROI are almost entirely the 6.88% trailing 5yr CAGR, which the repo's own backtest gives ~zero forward power and which this project has already stopped delivering: +1.1% over the trailing 12 months, 2025H1 $1,538 -> 2026H1 $1,561 psf (+1.5%); momentum -1.0. I override to 4.0%/yr (D18/OCR baseline 4.2% trimmed for this layout's standing inventory). Yield is also overstated: the $4,400 rent is the all-3BR average dominated by 1,065-1,173 sqft units; the 893 sqft layout asks $3,900-$4,300 and EdgeProp puts the project at 3.4%, so call it ~3.6-3.7% gross, not 4.06%. Against the owner's mandate - resale profit on a 5-7yr hold - the exit is the problem: this is a 2+study marketed as a 3BR, i.e. the least differentiated unit for the family buyers who are the natural bid for a 3BR, and it must clear eight competing asks ($1.30M-$1.52M) against ~5 same-band prints a year (~1.5yrs of standing inventory), while D'Nest next door prints a genuine 936 sqft 3BR at $1.32-1.44M. At 4.0%/yr a $1.30M entry plus $40.1k BSD exits around $1.64M in 6 years, ~5%/yr all-in with carry - respectable, not a reason to act. Note the entry-cost model assumes FIRST property; 20% ABSD ($260k) on a second property kills the case outright. Strengths (verified entry discount, OCR, 892-unit + 1,804-unit-enclave liquidity, 83yr lease, reputable Hong Realty/CDL build, positive resident reviews, no defect history found, $500k of budget left over) and concerns (fair-not-cheap vs district, mislabelled product, layout oversupply, flat tape, 13-min unsheltered MRT walk) genuinely balance. Neutral. LOCATION ADDENDUM (routed and sourced after the first pass): the walk is 962m / ~13 min unsheltered with two signalised crossings, and there is no bus stop on Pasir Ris Grove itself. The TPE sits 95-284m from the blocks and is the only expressway serving Pasir Ris - the one genuinely unresolved negative, with no measured dB reading, so visit at 8am and 6pm before offering. White Sands is being sold (S$467m to Growth Capital) with its AEI capital redirected to NEX and Hougang Mall, so there is no mall-upgrade catalyst. Against that, CR5 Pasir Ris is confirmed CRL Phase 1 for 2030, the integrated transport hub opened Apr-2025, Paya Lebar Air Base relocates from 2030, and the estate's commonly-cited negatives (Sungei Api Api, the old farmway, industrial odour, beach water) all de-escalate on inspection. Net location read: slightly worse than the first pass, not enough to move the rating. Neutral stands.
red_flags: The '3BR' is a 2+study, 2-bath 893 sqft layout (99.co/EdgeProp) - the weakest product to resell into the family-buyer pool that is the natural exit bid for a 3-bedroom

Eight competing compact-3BR asks live in this project right now ($1.30M-$1.52M for 872-894 sqft) against only ~5 same-size-band URA prints per year - roughly 1.5 years of standing inventory in this exact layout
D'Nest, the adjacent project sharing the Pasir Ris Grove site (1,804 units combined), prints a LARGER 936 sqft 3BR at $1.32M-$1.44M - near-identical money for 43 more sqft and two years newer

Project appreciation has flat-lined: +1.1% over the trailing 12 months and 2025H1 $1,538 -> 2026H1 $1,561 psf (+1.5%); momentum -1.0. The 6.88%/yr 5yr CAGR driving the algo's 795 score and 7.1% ROI is entirely backloaded to 2021-2024

Reported 4.06% gross yield is optimistic - it uses the all-3BR average rent of $4,400 (52 URA contracts, mostly 1,065-1,173 sqft units). This layout asks $3,900-$4,300; true gross is ~3.6-3.7% (EdgeProp puts the project at 3.4%)
Vs age-adjusted D18 peers the unit is only -0.4% (dead fair value) - the single strongest backtested forward lever is neutral here; the discount is intra-project only

Floor and facing are 0% populated in this DB (known broken enricher) and no stack profile has been researched, so the unit's floor, view and orientation are entirely unverified - the discount could partly be a bottom-floor or block-facing-block artifact
Seller cut $1.35M -> $1.30M within days of the 20-Jul listing (relisted from id 500184748) - motivated seller, or an unseen unit-specific defect

Fresh Pasir Ris supply keeps arriving: three new launches 2024-25, two more GLS residential sites released for 2026-27, and Coastal Cabana EC launching late-2026/early-2027 - all competing for the same OCR upgrader pool

MRT access confirmed worse than the 720m straight line: OSM/OSRM routing gives 962m / ~13 min from blk 115 and 1,064m / ~14 min from blk 111 to Pasir Ris MRT Exit B, unsheltered with two signalised crossings. Marketing '770m' claims are false. There is also NO bus stop on Pasir Ris Grove itself - nearest are 223-292m away but served only by routes 15/15A/46; the useful trunk stops are 320-350m

The TPE runs 95m from block 111 (149m from the site centroid, 284m at the farthest block) and is the ONLY expressway serving Pasir Ris, so peak congestion has no alternative route. No measured dB reading exists - a physical site visit at 8am and 6pm is warranted before any offer
Single access road: The Palette shares its one Pasir Ris Grove entrance with Coco Palms, NV Residences and Ripple Bay, and flow may worsen as that cluster builds out

White Sands will NOT be upgraded - Frasers Centrepoint Trust agreed in 2026 to sell it for S$467m to Growth Capital and redirected its AEI capital to NEX (~S$90m, from Q2 2026) and Hougang Mall. The new owner has announced no refurbishment, so the nearest mall is a no-catalyst asset
catalysts: Verified entry discount: $1.30M is below all five same-layout URA prints of the last 15 months ($1,350k-$1,370k) and below the low-floor print - roughly a 5% head start, confirmed on a 9-print cohort

Cross Island Line CR5 Pasir Ris is firmly CRL PHASE 1, target 2030 - S$980m contract awarded, station box 47m deep (2nd-deepest in Singapore), ~16 of 29 Phase 1 tunnel drives complete. CP2 Elias follows on the 2032 Punggol Extension, and DTL3e terminates at Sungei Bedok in 2H 2026. The dates are firm, but per the repo's backtest the future-infrastructure score has zero measured forward power - treat as narrative, not edge
$1.30M is an entry-level quantum for 3BR-labelled OCR stock, sitting in the deep HDB-upgrader bid, and leaves ~$500k of the owner's $1.8M budget unused
OCR is the region with the strongest realized forward returns in the full-panel backtest (+3.7%/yr vs RCR +3.1%, CCR +1.9%)
Deep, liquid book: 206 URA prints (~37/yr), 892 units in a 1,804-unit twin enclave with D'Nest, and this layout is the project's second-most-traded
Wide resale-to-new-launch gap: Pasir Ris 8 prints $2,072 psf and Parktown Residence $2,321 psf against The Palette's $1,548 - implied fair value from new launches is $1,684 psf (-13.6%)
Reputable build (Hong Realty / CDL, Architects 61, TOP 2015), positive resident reviews, no defect or MCST dispute history found in research

Pasir Ris integrated transport hub opened 27 Apr 2025 (air-conditioned, inside Pasir Ris 8) with the polyclinic at 6 Pasir Ris Dr 8 - the estate's amenity gravity is now firmly at Pasir Ris Central, ~1km from this site
Paya Lebar Air Base relocates from 2030, removing the RSAF aircraft noise that affects the estate (the overflights are RSAF, not Changi commercial)

Commonly-feared estate negatives do not hold up: Sungei Api Api is 425-584m away with no canal-facing units and no record of flooding on Pasir Ris Grove; Pasir Ris Farmway was cleared by 2018 and sits 2.1-2.8km away; industrial estates are 2.8-3.3km behind the town centre; NEA lifted the beach swimming advisory on 24 Jan 2025 and graded Pasir Ris Beach 'Good'; there is no columbarium or cemetery in the town

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: Solid but ordinary. URA logged 52 three-bedroom contracts at The Palette in 12 months (168 project-wide), so tenant demand is real and the unit will let. But the $4,400 figure in factual_data is the all-3BR average, skewed by the 1,065-1,173 sqft units; live asks for this exact 893 sqft layout run $3,900-$4,300, so budget ~$4,000/mo and ~3.6-3.7% gross (~2.2% net), against EdgeProp's 3.4% project-wide read. The 13-minute unsheltered MRT walk is a mild drag on transit-driven tenants; the Pasir Ris/Tampines employment belt and schools carry occupancy. Per the backtest, count this as carry only - high yield predicts LOWER forward price growth, so it is income, never an appreciation argument.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: I reject the 6.88%/yr in factual_data as the forward number. It is a 5-year trailing CAGR backloaded to 2021-2024 (project median psf $1,119 -> $1,433 over 2021-24, then $1,544 in 2025 and $1,561 in 2026H1); URA's own reading is appreciation_1yr = +1.1% with momentum -1.0. Per the repo's priors trailing CAGR has ~zero forward power and momentum is flat-to-contrarian, so I extrapolate neither: I use the D18/OCR baseline of 4.2% trimmed to 4.0%/yr for this layout's standing inventory. On that rate a $1.30M entry (+$40.1k BSD, first property) exits near $1.64M in six years, ~3%/yr net of a 2% exit commission, ~5%/yr with rental carry. The 5% entry discount is worth roughly 1.2 extra years of that rate up front - the single best thing about this deal. The wide resale-to-new-launch gap ($1,548 vs $2,072-$2,321 psf) supports the floor; the two 2026-27 Pasir Ris GLS sites and Coastal Cabana EC cap the ceiling.
agent_evaluation.stack_notes: UNKNOWN and this materially limits the call. No profile exists for The Palette (`stack_profile.status: not_researched`) and floor_level/facing are 0% populated in this DB - a known broken enricher - so I cannot say whether this is a 3rd-storey block-facing-block unit or a 15th-storey unit with the reservoir/greenery outlook. I therefore priced the discount against the worst case: the project's own floor factors are low 0.958 / mid 1.00 / high 1.044 across 46 prints, so a bottom-band unit is worth ~$1,467 psf = $1,310k - the $1.30M ask still clears it, and the May-25 893.4 sqft print on floors 1-5 was $1,350k. Stacked Homes notes the outer blocks 'face their neighbours' with little view but are sheltered from road noise. Run /research-development "The Palette" and confirm the actual floor and stack before any offer; a verified mid-to-high floor would move this toward Buy. Block matters here beyond the view: the TPE is 95m from blk 111 versus 284m at the farthest block, and the Park View Primary 1km MOE rule is block-dependent (998m from blk 111 = inside; 1,078m from blk 117 = outside). Elias Park Primary 543m, Coral Primary 675m and Meridian Secondary 545m are safely inside for all blocks.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_rate_source: D18/OCR district baseline 4.2%/yr trimmed to 4.0% for this layout's standing inventory. Resale-to-resale basis: 206 URA resale prints at The Palette show median psf $1,119 (2021) -> $1,433 (2024) -> $1,544 (2025) -> $1,561 (2026H1), i.e. +1.1% over the trailing 12 months and +1.5% 2025H1->2026H1. The 6.88% 5yr CAGR is backloaded to the 2021-24 run and is rejected as the forward number per the backtest's ~zero forward power for trailing CAGR. Dated catalyst: CRL Phase 1 Pasir Ris interchange ~2030, CRL Punggol Extension + Elias station ~2032.

history.summary: This is a ground-floor patio unit with an enclosable PES (private enclosed space), not a large 3BR or a 4BR. The 1,389 sqft strata area is a 3-bedroom tower layout (most likely the C1b 1,055-1,066 sqft type, possibly the C2a 3BR+study at 1,152-1,173 sqft) plus about 216-334 sqft of garden. Benchmarked against its real format, $2.00M carries a PES premium of 10-21% over the tower layout. That sits in the upper half of what this project's ground-floor units have actually fetched (+7%, +16%, +28%), so the headline '-6.6% vs URA median' is the garden being priced at full indoor psf, not value. For a 5-7yr investment the unit buys garden space that rents for little extra (about 2.9% gross), exits into a niche ground-floor buyer pool where this exact size has never printed, and has sat at ~$2.0M since early June.
history.rating_rationale:
FORMAT FIRST. Two independent listings (SRX, EdgeProp) and both detail-enriched PG listings describe this as a 'rare ground floor 1,389 sqft ... patio unit with enclosable PES, 3 bedroom'. The Palette's published mix gives 3-Bedroom as 1,055-1,410 sqft and 3BR+Study as 1,152-1,528, with ground-floor PES variants such as C2a-1(P2) at 1,518 and D1-1(P2) at 1,787. The 4BR D1 tower layout is 1,378 sqft internal and landlords file it as 4BR (22 URA rental contracts at 1,300-1,400 sqft). So bed_bands' '4BR band' read is a size coincidence: this is a 3-bedder plus a garden. 1,389 sqft (129 sqm) has never printed in 193 URA Palette transactions since late 2021. 

WRONG COHORT. MMR's 'same-size' comps (min $1,495 psf, flag ask_below_stack_prints) are 4BR and dual-key TOWER units at 1,378/1,399/1,410 sqft, which printed $2.18-2.25M in 2025-26. Those are the wrong comparison. 

RIGHT COHORT. Same-format tower prints over the last 12 months: 1,055-1,066 sqft median ~$1.65M ($1,530-1,600 psf); 1,152-1,173 sqft median ~$1.82M. Ground-floor PES premiums this project has actually paid over the base layout are +7% (1,335 sqft, Feb-24, $1.65M), +16% (1,367 sqft, Oct-23, $1.648M) and +28% (1,410 sqft, Dec-25, $2.108M, the closest analog). Other PES variants paid +0-14% (1,518 sqft +14%; 1,798 sqft +1-10%; 1,001 sqft +9%). The ask implies +21% over C1b, or +10% over C2a. Fair value is roughly $1.80-1.95M if the base is C1b and $1.90-2.05M if it is C2a. At best the ask is fair; it is never a discount. 

On internal area the ask is $1,705-1,876 psf, which is +16% to +28% vs the age-adjusted D18 median. Re-scored on that basis, score_1000 falls from 715 to 574 (C2a) or 462 (C1b), below the 650 gate. Those re-scores treat the garden as worth nothing, so they are a lower bound. Either way, the 715 that passed the gate rests on the artifact. 

MARKET VERDICT. A 1,389 sqft ask at $2.00M has been on PG since 7 Jun 2026 across five agents (one tried $2.22M in Aug, then it came back to $1.99-2.00M). In the same window two 1,378 sqft tower 4BRs printed $2.25M (Jun-26) and $2.20M (Aug-26). Buyers are not treating this unit as 4BR money. 

WHAT HOLDS UP is all project-level: OCR region; a deep, liquid 892-unit book (193 URA prints in 5yr); REALSCORE 4.2 with 98.6% of 440 resale pairs profitable (433 vs 7) over a 7.6yr average hold, which is strong downside evidence. But those owners mostly entered at $1,000-1,400 psf. A garden premium paid at the top of its observed range gets no protection from that record. 

Avoid at medium confidence. Confidence is not high because the exact base layout (C1b vs C2a) is unconfirmed and the Dec-25 $2.108M ground-floor print shows a garden-seeking buyer can pay this much.
red_flags: Format: ground-floor PES/patio unit. The 1,389 sqft strata includes about 216-334 sqft of enclosable garden. The internal layout is a 3-bedroom (most likely C1b 1,055-1,066 sqft, possibly C2a 3BR+study 1,152-1,173), not the 1,378 sqft D1 4BR it shares a size band with

The -6.6% vs URA median, -1.8% vs age-adjusted D18 median, and the 'below all 6 same-size prints' discount are all artifacts. The comps are 4BR and dual-key tower units ($2.18-2.25M). On internal area the ask is $1,705-1,876 psf, +16% to +28% vs age-adjusted district peers

The ask implies a garden premium of +21% over the C1b tower layout (~$1.65M, 12-month prints) or +10% over C2a (~$1.82M). That is in the upper half of what Palette ground-floor units have fetched (+7%, +16%, +28% for 3BR-type PES variants)

Zero URA prints at 1,389 sqft / 129 sqm in 193 Palette transactions since late 2021. Only ~13 PES-variant prints of any type in 5 years (~2-3/yr). The exit is into a niche 'ground floor lovers' sub-pool, with a wide price range (+0% to +28% over base), so exit price is very uncertain

Stale ask: a 1,389 sqft unit at ~$2.00M has been listed since 7 Jun 2026 by at least five agents (Gabriel Shaun, Louis Koh, Chris Lim $1.99M, Mira Kelyna, plus an unattributed listing; one interim $2.22M try). Two of them, likely the same unit, are both tagged blk 113 / Ground Floor. Four months unsold while 4BR towers cleared at $2.20-2.25M
Note on price history: the 'price_history' chain (2.00 -> 2.22 -> 2.00M) links different agents' listings through unit_group 'the palette|3|365'. It is not one unit's repricing history

Weak carry: the garden earns little extra rent. URA 3BR contracts in the 1,300-1,500 sqft bands (the PES 3BRs) run $4,500-5,400 against $4,200-4,500 for tower 3BRs. At ~$4,800/mo gross yield is ~2.9% and net ~1.8%. The dossier's $4,400 (2.64%) is the all-3BR average

Project tape is flat: C1b 3BR median ~$1.61-1.64M in late 2024 vs ~$1.65M in 2026; D1 4BR $2.23M (Mar-25) vs $2.20-2.25M (2026); momentum -0.9. The 6.72%/yr 5yr CAGR behind MMR's biggest component (appreciation +8.16) was earned in 2021-24 and has no measured forward power

Ground-floor-specific exposures cannot be checked from this data: block, facing, TPE proximity (the TPE runs ~95 m from blk 111 per the prior eval), pool/carpark-adjacent noise, privacy, damp and insects. Floor is 'Ground Floor' per two PG listings; the claimed blk 113 may be the project's default address

Walk to Pasir Ris MRT is ~1 km and unsheltered (962-1,064 m routed, per the 2026-07-29 eval), not the advertised 750 m. The CRL interchange is due ~2030; the future-infra score has no measured forward power
Pasir Ris supply keeps coming: Pasir Ris 8 ($2,072 psf), further GLS sites, and Coastal Cabana EC, all competing for the same HDB-upgrader pool
Mandate fit: over 'his' $1.8M ceiling. Within 'hers' ~$2.5M, but for $2.20-2.25M she can buy a real 1,378 sqft tower 4BR (D1) in the same project, which is the better use of a 3-4BR budget
catalysts: OCR region: the strongest realized forward region in the full-panel backtest (+3.7%/yr vs RCR +3.1%, CCR +1.9%)

Strong downside record on a deep sample: REALSCORE 4.2/5, 98.6% of 440 resale pairs profitable (433 vs 7), average annualized 5.3%, average hold 7.6 yrs, 58% HDB-upgrader buyers. Well above the 150-resale trust bar
Deep, liquid project: 892 units, 193 URA prints in ~5 yrs, $1.3B+ transacted. Buyer-pool depth survives clustering in the backtest

Closest physical analog supports the seller: a 1,410 sqft ground-floor unit (floor 01-05) sold for $2.108M in Dec-25. A garden-seeking family buyer can pay this much; the question is whether the next one will
Two agents are marketing what is likely the same ground-floor unit at $1.99M and $2.00M, so there is room to negotiate toward the ~$1.85-1.90M where a C1b-based PES unit would be fairly priced

Reputable build (Hong Realty / CDL, Architects 61, TOP 2015-16) with no defect or MCST dispute history found in prior research. Cross Island Line CR5 Pasir Ris is due ~2030 (narrative, not a measured edge)

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: Tenants pay for bedrooms, not gardens. URA rental filings at The Palette show 3BR contracts in the 1,000-1,100 sqft band at a $4,200 median (95 contracts) and 1,100-1,200 sqft at $4,500 (66). The larger 3BR bands that match PES units run 1,300-1,400 sqft at $4,500-4,900 and 1,400-1,500 sqft at $4,600-5,400 (5 contracts). A realistic rent for this unit is about $4,600-5,000/mo, or 2.8-3.0% gross and ~1.7-1.9% net on $2.0M, versus ~3.3% project-wide (realsmart, 102 contracts). The rental market is deep (537 URA contracts), so vacancy risk is low, but the garden premium is uncompensated carry. Counted as carry only; high yield predicts lower price growth anyway.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: Trailing 6.72%/yr (5yr, 193 prints) was earned in 2021-24; the tape has been flat for ~18 months for both the 3BR (C1b ~$1.61M to ~$1.65M) and 4BR (~$2.23M to $2.20-2.25M) formats, with momentum -0.9. Under current priors that trailing rate carries no forward weight. The forward drivers are region (OCR, positive) and value, and value here is negative once the PES area is stripped out. Forward expectation is roughly the OCR baseline (~3-4%/yr) on the indoor part, with extra variance on the garden premium. Ground-floor premiums at this project have ranged from 0% to +28%, so a buyer paying near the top carries asymmetric downside at exit. No override applied.
agent_evaluation.stack_notes: Ground floor ('Ground Floor' on both detail-enriched PG listings, 500221257 and 500270699, which are likely one unit marketed by two agents). Block is claimed as 113, but that may be the project's default address, so treat it as unverified. Facing is unobtainable from PG. No profile exists for The Palette (profiles/ has none), and stacks/facings were not researched in this run: the verdict turns on format and price, which a stack profile would not change. Most likely layout is C1b-x(P) (3BR, 2 bath, 1,055-1,066 sqft internal + ~323-334 sqft PES), possibly C2a(P) (3BR+study, 3 bath, 1,152-1,173 internal + ~216-237 PES). Listings disagree on 2 vs 3 baths, and the floor plan would settle it. Prior research: outer blocks face neighbouring condos (NV Residences, D'Nest, Elias Green); the TPE is ~95-284 m from the blocks; one shared Pasir Ris Grove entrance. A ground-floor unit facing the TPE side or the carpark ramp would be a further discount at exit. Inspect before any offer.
